newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico resort hotel denies weekend Salinas visit.
newsitem.headline: Mexico resort hotel denies weekend Salinas visit.

text.p: The manager of a Pacific coast resort hotel denied on Monday news reports that disgraced former president Carlos Salinas de Gortari had spent a weekend at his establishment.

Local media reported on Sunday that Salinas, who fled Mexico in March 1995 after his brother was arrested on murder charges and the economy collapsed, spent the weekend at the Quinta Real hotel in the tourist resort of Huatulco, 350 miles (560 km) southeast of Mexico City.
"This is not true. It was all was the result of a mix-up ... there was bad information," Jose Luis Muno, the manager of the Quinta Real, told Reuters in a telephone interview from Huatulco.
He said the confusion arose because a businessman from Mexico City registered at his hotel in the name of "Carlos de Gortari." The guest had "nothing to do with the former president," he added.

Mexican media had reported that Salinas, who currently lives in self-imposed exile in Dublin, held weekend meetings at the hotel with Mario Ramon Beteta, the former director of state oil monopoly Pemex.
But Muno said this speculation arose from the name of the businessman's wife -- Fernanda Beteta.
Salinas de Gortari has not been sighted in Mexico since his March 1995 departure, though he has surfaced in the United States, Canada and Cuba on visits and brief stays.

Though adored by most Mexicans toward the end of his 1988-94 term, the economic collapse and wave of corruption scandals which broke after Salinas left office have turned most citizens strongly against him.
Salinas's brother Raul remains under arrest in the maximum security Almoloya jail outside Mexico City awaiting trial on murder and illicit enrichment charges, which he has denied.
